summary: All 8 handover REDs pass and nothing else moved. T10R3-F-001 (re-walk crash safety) is fixed by peek-and-advance: Profile.takeMailboxRewalk (read+delete) became pendingMailboxRewalk (read only), keepMailboxRewalk is now called once per FULLY JUDGED page from inbound.ts's page loop, and a new finishMailboxRewalk deletes the key in exactly one place - when the relay reports next_cursor === null, i.e. the walk reached the end of the mailbox. The try/catch restoration and the post-loop write are gone because nothing is ever taken away. The invariant is that a single store transaction REPLACES position P(k-1) with P(k), so durable storage always holds a position at or behind where the walk truly got to; there is no interval an interruption can fall into, and an interruption anywhere costs the repeated judging of at most one page. The T6-F-004 trap was NOT taken: the position is still cleared, on exactly the same condition as before, and both guards say so - rewalk-crash-safety case 4 (0 of the pages after a completed re-walk restart at poison index 0; 3 ordinary polls cost <= 6 pages; history == 1) and flood-closure RED-4b (an ordinary poll presents no cursor) are green. T10R3-F-002 is fixed by T14's shape/range split, not a special-case code: decodeReadThroughShape stays ahead of authorisation (the malformed-shapes test demands 400 INVALID_SCHEMA independent of who asks), and readThroughWithinIssued moved to AFTER VerifyMessageSignature on the ack route, matching the poll route. An unverified caller never reaches the range check, so every ladder value answers one uniform 403 and the binary search has nothing to compare. T10R3-F-003 is fixed by one shared predicate in the new product file apps/cli/src/transport/loopback.ts, imported by both RelayClient and parseClientConfig; RelayClient's /^127\./ prefix rule is gone and the shared rule is the STRICTER original, so 127.0.0.1, 127.9.9.9, localhost and [::1] keep working. MATRIX on Node v26.5.0 (non-login default): pnpm typecheck exit 0; pnpm lint exit 0 (no package defines one); pnpm test exit 0, 50 files / 293 tests / 293 passed / 0 failed; pnpm --filter @echolet/cli test:e2e exit 0, 3/3; go -C apps/relay test ./... untagged, -tags relayv2, -race, and -race -tags relayv2 each exit 0 with 8 packages ok, 0 failures and 0 DATA RACE; go vet exit 0. No test file was modified: all five T15 digests are byte-identical to T15's recorded values. No schema or Go validation was relaxed; the test count is unchanged at 293, so nothing was added, skipped, narrowed or deleted. DONE_WITH_CONCERNS for the residuals only, chiefly T15-F-003's coverage bound (one interruption point, one ciphertext regime) which the verifier should sweep, and stale prose in two test files naming takeMailboxRewalk which I may not edit.

acceptance.criterion: The re-walk position is never absent from durable storage while a walk that owns it is in flight. State plainly where it is written, where it is cleared, and why no interruption can fall between them.
acceptance.evidence: WRITTEN in two places: commands/cli.ts -> Profile.requestMailboxRewalk() at contact import (the value "0", the head), and inbound.ts's page loop -> Profile.keepMailboxRewalk(batch.next_cursor), once per page the walk received and FULLY judged. CLEARED in one place: Profile.finishMailboxRewalk(), called from the same loop only when batch.next_cursor === null - the walk was offered and judged every envelope the mailbox holds. NO INTERRUPTION CAN FALL BETWEEN THEM because there is no 'between': the old shape was a removal and a later restoration with the whole walk in the gap; the new shape is ONE store transaction per page that replaces position P(k-1) with P(k). Before commit the store holds P(k-1), after commit P(k); it never holds nothing. A judgement interrupted part-way through a page has not advanced the position, so that page is re-offered rather than skipped (also the R-4 direction). Death after the last page's commits but before finishMailboxRewalk leaves the position one page back, costing one re-walked page. Section 1.3 of t16-implementation-report.md.

acceptance.criterion: The F-012 store-identity guarantee is preserved: an ordinary poll with no re-walk pending still leaves the encrypted store byte-identical. Show this rather than asserting it.
acceptance.evidence: Shown two ways. (1) The repository's own measurement: apps/cli/src/runtime/inbound.readMark.test.ts snapshots EVERY key and value of the encrypted store (snapshot(), lines 91-96) before a poll that accepts nothing and asserts toEqual(before) afterwards; its cast() never calls requestMailboxRewalk, so that poll is exactly 'ordinary, no re-walk pending'. It is green on this tree: '✓ src/runtime/inbound.readMark.test.ts (2 tests) 5476ms' with '... acknowledges no envelope and mutates nothing, but advances the read position'. (2) End to end: flood-closure RED-4b, green (2.8s), proves that after a re-walk ran to the end of the mailbox the next poll presents NO cursor, i.e. the client holds no read position of its own. At code level pendingMailboxRewalk() contains no tx.set and no tx.delete, so the re-walk path of an ordinary poll performs no store mutation whatsoever.

findings.problem: The re-walk crash-safety suite exercises a single interruption point (the CLI held on its third poll page) and a single ciphertext regime (4-byte minimum, so the page boundary is the client's poll_batch_size rather than the relay's byte budget). Other interruption points - inside accept() between two envelopes of one page, between the last page's commits and finishMailboxRewalk(), inside ackPending() - and the maximum-size-ciphertext regime are argued correct but not measured.
findings.impact: A crash-safety property that holds at one interruption point is weaker evidence than the finding it closes deserves. A regression at an unmeasured point would reproduce T10R3-F-001 for a narrower set of crashes and no test would notice.
findings.suggested_fix: The verifier should sweep at least the two structurally distinct points named above and one maximum-size-ciphertext world, reusing the existing counting proxy's hold mechanism. This carries T15-F-003 forward rather than restating it; it is a coverage bound the tests-creator accepted deliberately, not a defect introduced here.
findings.evidence: rewalk-crash-safety.test.ts interruptPollAtPage(3, ...) is the only interruption used by cases 1-3, and primeLateImport floods with ciphertextBytes = 4 in every world. T15's own result recorded this as T15-F-003 and kept its status at DONE_WITH_CONCERNS for it.

findings.problem: A poll interrupted while a re-walk is in flight now leaves the position ADVANCED rather than absent, so the next poll presents a cursor where before it presented none.
findings.impact: This is the intended behaviour change and is exactly what flood-closure RED-4 was re-stated to permit. It is recorded so that a future reader of RED-4b does not generalise 'an ordinary poll is cursorless' into 'every poll after a crash is cursorless' and re-introduce the defect while trying to protect F-012.
findings.suggested_fix: None. RED-4b already pins the narrow property where it holds: a poll with NO re-walk pending presents no cursor.
findings.evidence: flood-closure.test.ts lines 588-650 record the orchestrator's three-part ruling verbatim; RED-4 and RED-4b are both green on this tree.

findings.problem: Two concurrent poll() invocations against the SAME profile directory from two processes are not serialised by this change (they were not before it either). Both would advance the one cli:mailbox-rewalk key.
findings.impact: The safety invariant still holds for each walk - the key only ever moves to a position some walk genuinely received and judged, so nothing is skipped - but the slower walk may find the position further ahead than it left it and re-walk less than it expected. No message is lost; the cost is only that one of the two walks does redundant work.
findings.suggested_fix: Out of scope for this task. If concurrent same-profile polls are ever supported, the store's single-writer transaction is the place to serialise, not the page loop.
findings.evidence: EncryptedSqliteStore.transaction is the only mutation boundary and is per-process; InboundMessenger.serial() orders operations within one process only.
